paper_id: Wang et al. - 2010 - ETOC Obtaining robustness in component-based localization
title: ETOC: Obtaining Robustness in Component-based Localization
motivation: Component-based localization outperforms node-based in sparse networks but is highly sensitive to ranging errors causing structural deformation
problem_framing: Define error tolerance as upper bound of ranging errors under which a component can be localized uniquely without deformation
key_insight: A single node suffers only translation, but components suffer three transformations (translation, rotation, reflection), requiring new robust patterns beyond existing flip-ambiguity methods
method_signature: ETOC uses robust coordinate system conversion patterns to achieve guaranteed localization robustness
evaluation_criteria: Performance (localized node ratio), accuracy (SPEE), cost (trilaterations per node)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Case 4 requires five edges while optimal pattern requires four; parallel line special case has zero error tolerance and is non-robust
evidence_for_taste: the SPEE of RQ is always higher
ETOC performs better in error control
requires the average degree to be over 25
the cost of ETOC is near optimal
thinking_moves: Identify that components have higher DOF than single nodes (3 transformations vs 1)
Define error tolerance analytically to bound structural deformation
Exploit geometry of robust patterns to eliminate ambiguities systematically
Distinguish node-based vs component-based error tolerance requirements
